issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a public constructor SealSaloon(String) that takes a saloon name, but the provided Solution implements a no-argument constructor SealSaloon() and the Template's Main (example usage) also calls new SealSaloon() with no parameter. This constructor-parameter mismatch can confuse students about the required API and cause tests or expected usage to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the constructor signature across artifacts. Either (A) update the Solution and the Template Main to provide and use a public SealSaloon(String name) constructor (and preserve any internal initialization), or (B) modify the problem statement and UML to accept a no-argument constructor (SealSaloon()) and clarify that the saloon name is optional. Prefer option (A) to match the UML and problem text: change the constructor in SealSaloon to public SealSaloon(String name) and update example usages to call new SealSaloon("SomeName").

issues.description: The problem statement (and UML) specifies a SealSaloon constructor that takes a String parameter (SealSaloon(String)) and explicitly states the constructor takes the saloon name. However, both the template usage (Main.java) and the solution implement and use a parameterless constructor (SealSaloon()). This signature mismatch between the specification and the provided code can confuse students about the required constructor signature and where to supply the saloon name.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor requirement consistent across artifacts. Either: (A) Update the template and solution to provide a constructor taking a String (public SealSaloon(String name)) and adjust all usages (or overload with a no-arg constructor delegating to the new one), or (B) revise the problem statement/UML to require a parameterless constructor. Preferred: implement public SealSaloon(String name) in code (and optionally keep a no-arg overload) so the implementation matches the specification.
